scope: Complete delivery architecture for the six acquisition artifacts and the separate Workspace provisioning model governed by R09.
boundary: This architecture is a build contract, not a release claim. No artifact becomes purchasable, licensed, downloadable, maintained, or supported until its named package and every universal and artifact-specific acceptance test pass in production. Workspace remains unavailable until its separate capability and authorization gates pass.

versionPolicy.immutableReleaseRule: A fulfilled release is immutable. Corrections or source updates create a new version and changelog entry; the receipt and manifest preserve the version acquired.

prohibitedUses: representation as legal, medical, compliance, or platform assurance
requiredTerms: licensee identity and seat or organization scope

acquisitionArchitecture.fulfillmentContract: Successful payment creates one immutable order record, identifies the exact licensed version, sends a receipt and time-bounded download delivery, and permits verified redelivery without creating a second order.
acquisitionArchitecture.securityAndPrivacy: Use a hosted PCI-compliant payment provider; store no raw card data; minimize purchaser data; disclose processors, retention, support use, and deletion limits; sign download URLs; prevent object enumeration; rate-limit redelivery.
acquisitionArchitecture.failureContract: A failed, abandoned, duplicated, delayed, or refunded transaction must show a recoverable state, create no contradictory entitlement, and preserve an auditable event record without exposing payment secrets.
acquisitionArchitecture.supportContract: Receipt and product page identify support channel, response target, refund path, file-access recovery, current maintenance state, and what support does not include.

maintenanceArchitecture.requiredDisclosure: Every product states its source-review cutoff, maintenance state, next review trigger, update entitlement, and whether a new version is included or separately acquired.
maintenanceArchitecture.urgentCorrectionRule: Material safety, authority, calculation, rights, or security defects trigger withdrawal or a conspicuous correction and purchaser notice; silent file replacement is prohibited.

universalArtifactAcceptanceTests: Every file named in the manifest exists, opens in its declared format, and matches its SHA-256 checksum.
The package has a README, version manifest, changelog, license, rights/attribution record, accessibility note, support terms, maintenance disclosure, and professional-accountability boundary.
Examples, templates, formulas, schemas, prompts, and internal links are complete and resolve within the package.
All dated legal, regulatory, platform, pricing, scientific, and vendor claims identify their source-review cutoff and verification status.
A clean-device acquisition test completes checkout, receipt, authorized download, extraction, and first-use instructions for the exact version.
Failure, duplicate, expiry, redelivery, refund, and supersession states behave according to the acquisition contract.
Public copy, release registry, order record, delivered manifest, and downloaded files agree on artifact name, version, contents, license, price, maintenance, and availability.
No release language implies individualized advice, guaranteed compliance, guaranteed platform distribution, guaranteed outcomes, or continuing updates beyond the stated maintenance contract.

artifactAcceptanceTests: Build the worked example from an empty directory using only the package instructions.
Validate all example records against the supplied JSON schemas.
Trace every generated example claim to a source and approval record.
Confirm the 20 promised prompts and all five domains are present and indexed.
Confirm every neuroscience mechanism and platform constraint maps to a cited source and bounded claim.
Confirm all three promised worked examples and the complete twelve-minute template are present.
Run one unseen content brief through the framework and document each decision without claiming distribution or individual-response prediction.
Verify every platform-policy statement carries platform, URL, retrieval date, and current/unverified status.

artifacts.packageType: dated regulatory comparison and verification model
contents: Oregon, Colorado, and New Mexico source-pinned records
artifactAcceptanceTests: Recalculate every APQ score from documented inputs and obtain the published result.
Verify every operative date, fee, authority, and implementation-status statement against a cited primary source as of the cutoff.
Confirm unknown, proposed, unpublished, and nonbinding values cannot be scored as final facts.
Test the funder classifier on disclosed examples and preserve source and classification rationale.

artifacts.packageType: legal-authority intake, verification, and claim-record system
contents: Mata and Wadsworth worked failure analyses
artifactAcceptanceTests: Validate all fixtures against the supplied schema and reject missing authority, pinpoint, retrieval-date, confidence, or change-watch fields.
Process a disclosed primary-source set through all three stages and reproduce the final claim records.
Seed fabricated, nonbinding, superseded, and jurisdictionally irrelevant authorities and confirm each is blocked or accurately labeled.
Require human verification before any consequential output and state that the package is not a continuously connected feed.

artifacts.packageType: dated Oregon psilocybin operations and reporting kit
artifactAcceptanceTests: Qualified Oregon legal/compliance review confirms the dated source map and all required disclaimers before release.
Reconcile every field and definition against the current OPS form and governing authority at the source cutoff.
Run boundary-value and opt-out scenarios through totals and formulas without misclassification or double counting.
Confirm the calendar distinguishes official deadlines from internal targets and does not silently imply continuing legal updates.
Recalculate all sample baselines, control limits, and decision rules from raw fixtures.
Confirm every platform-policy statement has an official source, retrieval date, quotation/paraphrase label, and verification status.
Run normal variation, suspected reduction, and confirmed enforcement scenarios through the three-tier protocol.
Ensure outputs distinguish signal from proof and never promise diagnosis, appeal success, or restored distribution.

workspaceAccessArchitecture.commercialRelationship: Workspace access is a separately provisioned engagement, pilot, program, or licensed implementation; artifact acquisition creates no Workspace account or entitlement.

buildSequence: Freeze this architecture and keep every acquisition and Workspace state unavailable.
Build and independently accept one complete artifact package at a time.
Implement shared licensing, checkout, order, fulfillment, support, and maintenance infrastructure.
Run artifact-specific and universal clean-device acquisition tests before enabling that artifact.
Build Workspace identity, data, permissions, review, audit, and operational states as a separate program.
Enable only the individually proven artifact or Workspace capability; do not batch-promote the estate.
